name: Improper Input Validation (validation-bypass cluster)
expectedPluginsNote: Was eslint-plugin-secure-coding, and had been wrong since these fixtures landed in #290 — not broken by any later change. They are candidate-research fixtures, written for rules that were PLANNED for secure-coding; the rules were then built in browser-security instead (no-incomplete-url-sanitization, no-insecure-redirects, require-postmessage-origin-check), which is where a redirect allowlist, a postMessage origin test and a URL scheme check belong. The only secure-coding rule carrying CWE-020 is no-graphql-injection, which could never fire on a URL substring check. Every fixture here IS detected, with accurate messages, by the plugin now named. Safe to correct: expectedPlugins reaches ilb-cwe-corpus output metadata only and does not gate scoring — every plugin is run against every fixture — so this restates no published number.

vulnerable.description: Unescaped '.' in a hostname regexp used as a redirect allowlist
postMessage origin check with an unanchored regular expression
includes()/indexOf() substring match on a URL as an authorization decision
Scheme denylist blocking only 'javascript:', leaving data:/vbscript:/blob:
indexOf-emulated endsWith with no tail boundary (.trusted.com.evil.io passes)

safe.description: Hostname regexp with escaped dots and ^…$ anchoring
Fully anchored origin regexp for postMessage validation
new URL(url).hostname equality check with fail-closed parse handling
String.prototype.endsWith suffix check with explicit dot boundary
